fatal_errors: Changing elemental identities to vary atomic-size mismatch also changes elastic modulus, bonding, stacking-fault energy, phase stability, and electronic structure, so the proposed comparison does not isolate lattice distortion.
XRD peak broadening is not a unique measure of atomic-size-mismatch distortion; crystallite size, dislocation density, residual stress, and instrumental broadening can produce the same signal.
No supporting evidence is cited, and atom-probe tomography does not directly quantify lattice strain.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general strength-governing question and supplies a testable trend, boundary, and falsification rule. It is therefore scientifically plausible as a generic solid-solution-strengthening hypothesis. However, it does not reconstruct the target intervention or processing window: the target concerns milling-time and SPS-temperature control of nanocrystalline CoCrFeNiTi, with strengthening arising synergistically from Hall–Petch grain refinement, milling-induced dislocation density, solid-solution effects, densification, and an FCC/BCC phase mixture. The generated proposal instead assumes homogenized, single-phase alloys and varies elemental size mismatch. It consequently misses the cast baseline, HEBM/SPS conditions, nanocrystalline mediator, phase fractions, density, and quantitative hardness and compressive-strength outcomes. Its controlled comparison is also materially confounded, while the proposed XRD observable cannot uniquely establish the claimed mechanism without line-profile separation and complementary local-strain or dislocation measurements.
